course_name_original: STRUCTURAL MECHANICS AND PRINCIPLES OF MECHANICAL DESIGN I.C. (B031856)
course_name_en: STRUCTURAL MECHANICS AND PRINCIPLES OF MECHANICAL DESIGN I.C.
prerequisites: Knowledge acquired in the courses of Rational Mechanics and Mathematical Analysis.

learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide the necessary tools to address structural problems both in the design and verification phases. The objective is achieved through the study of some fundamental elements of solid mechanics (concepts of stress, strain, and constitutive relations) and their application to the analysis and verification of structures.

syllabus_topics: Characteristics and arrangement of supports, kinematics of constrained structures, statics of constrained structures.

Fundamental equations of statics, auxiliary equations, characteristics of stress, indefinite equilibrium equations for one-dimensional solids, determination of stress characteristics for statically determinate structures.

Tension test; Hooke	
				’s law, constitutive equation for axial strains, differential equation of the elastic line for axial strains.
Bending beam; constitutive equation for bending strains, differential equation of the elastic line for bending strains.
Virtual work theorem, calculation of displacements for isostatic structures.

Concept of stress, Cauchy	
				’s hypothesis, stress tensor, equilibrium equations, principal stresses and directions.
Infinitesimal strain tensor, strains and principal strain directions.
Elastic behavior of materials, isotropic linear elastic constitutive relation, elastic problem.
Torsion of compact, closed, and open sections
Tresca and Von Mises criteria, introduction to serviceability limit state and ultimate limit state
assessment_rules: The student’s level of learning and ability to critically discuss the structural aspects of some simple structures will be assessed through a written and an oral examination. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for excellent, in-depth knowledge and independent operation. Honors (Laude) is awarded for work distinguished by brilliance and originality.
bibliography: L. Gambarotta, L. Nunziante, A. Tralli, Scienza delle costruzioni, McGraw-Hill, Milano, 2003.
O. Belluzzi, Scienza delle Costruzioni, Vol. I, Zanichelli editore, Bologna, 1996.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica (Mechanical Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
